name: The miracles of Jesus
description: Ten days with the signs Jesus did: what each one shows about who He is.

days.title: Water into wine
days.note: Jesus' first sign, at a wedding.
days.devotional:
Jesus begins at a party, saving a family from embarrassment. His first sign is about joy and abundance.

He cares about ordinary needs as well as big ones.
days.prayer: Jesus, thank You for caring about the ordinary parts of my life.
questions: What does this first sign tell you about Jesus?
What ordinary need can you bring to Him?

days.title: A healing word
days.note: Jesus heals a boy from a distance.
days.devotional:
An official begs Jesus to come; Jesus simply says the boy will live. The man believes the word and goes home.

Jesus' word is enough.
days.prayer: Lord, help me trust Your word even before I see the answer.
questions: Where do you need to trust Jesus' word?
What helps you believe before you see?

days.title: Calming the storm
days.devotional:
The disciples ask who this could be, that even the wind obeys Him. The miracle points to His power over creation.

Nothing is outside His authority.
days.prayer: Jesus, You rule over every storm. I trust You with mine.
questions: What storm do you need Jesus to calm?
What does this sign show about who Jesus is?

days.title: Feeding the crowd
days.note: Five loaves and two fish feed thousands.
days.devotional:
A boy's small lunch becomes more than enough in Jesus' hands. There are even leftovers.

What we offer, however small, can be multiplied.
days.prayer: Lord, take what little I have and use it for others.
questions: What small thing could you offer Jesus?
Where have you seen God provide more than enough?

days.title: Walking on water
days.note: Jesus comes to His disciples on the sea.
days.devotional:
Peter walks while he looks at Jesus and sinks when he looks at the wind. Jesus catches him immediately.

Faith keeps its eyes on Jesus.
days.prayer: Jesus, keep my eyes on You, and catch me when I sink.
questions: What 'wind' distracts you from Jesus?
When has Jesus caught you?

days.title: Sight for the blind
days.note: A man born blind is healed, and questioned.
days.devotional:
Everyone argues about the miracle, but the man keeps it simple: he was blind and now he sees.

Your own story of what Jesus has done matters.
days.prayer: Jesus, open my eyes to see You more clearly.
questions: What has Jesus done in your life that you could share?
Where do you need clearer sight?

days.title: Touched and healed
days.note: A woman reaches for Jesus' cloak; a girl is raised.
days.devotional:
Jesus stops for the woman everyone ignored and calls her daughter. Then He goes on to a home where all hope seemed gone.

He is never too busy for the one who reaches out.
days.prayer: Jesus, I reach out to You today. Thank You for stopping for me.
questions: Which person in this story do you relate to?
What do you need to reach out to Jesus for?

days.title: Lazarus
days.note: Jesus weeps, then calls His friend out of the tomb.
days.devotional:
Jesus grieves with Mary and Martha before He acts. He is both deeply moved and fully powerful.

He is the One who gives life that death cannot hold.
days.prayer: Jesus, thank You for grieving with me and for the hope of resurrection.
questions: What does it mean to you that Jesus wept?
Where do you need His life-giving power?

days.title: A man let down through a roof
days.note: Friends carry a paralysed man to Jesus.
days.devotional:
Four friends won't let a crowd stop them. Jesus forgives the man's sins and then heals his body.

Faithful friends bring people to Jesus.
days.prayer: Lord, make me a friend who brings others to You.
questions: Who has carried you to Jesus?
Who could you help bring to Him?

days.title: The greatest sign
days.devotional:
Every miracle points here. Jesus Himself rises from the dead, and the women are the first to hear.

Because He lives, every other promise holds.
days.prayer: Risen Jesus, thank You for the hope of the empty tomb.
questions: Which miracle this week meant the most to you?
How does the resurrection change your day?
